fields.title: AVENIO Bremen
fields.description:
The AVENIO Bremen Project is a significant collaboration between Siemens and the German operator Bremer Straßenbahn AG (BSAG). The project began when BSAG ordered a new tram fleet for the Free Hanseatic City of Bremen from Siemens. This order consisted of 67 Avenio trams and included an option for up to 17 additional trams. The delivery of the four-section trains to Bremen’s tram network was scheduled to begin in the spring of 2019.

Later, BSAG decided to order an additional ten Avenio trams from Siemens, exercising an option in the contract signed in June 2017. This increased the total number of Siemens trams in the Hanseatic city’s fleet to 77.

The Avenio trams are easily identifiable as a new member of the BSAG fleet. They feature the company’s signature bright red paint and references to the linear design and the BSAG logo used on earlier trams. The interior design of the Avenio trams is also noteworthy. It allows speedy boarding and alighting, which shortens stops at the stations. Large windows and LED lighting provide pleasant lighting conditions. Riders with reduced mobility in wheelchairs or with walkers have spacious areas available at the entrances with convenient seating or room for parking. An electric lift at the second door operates a complete section of the floor.

This project represents a significant milestone for mass transit in Bremen and the surrounding region.

fields.title: AVENIO Copenhagen
fields.description:
The AVENIO Copenhagen Project is a significant collaboration between Siemens and the Danish urban transport development company, Greater Copenhagen Light Rail I/S. In a consortium with the general infrastructure contractor Per Aarsleff A/S, Siemens received an order to build a light rail system in Copenhagen, Denmark.

The contract includes 27 four-car Avenio trams, rail electrification, signalling, communication, workshop equipment, overall project management, and system integration. The project is being implemented as a turnkey solution. In addition, the contract includes maintenance services for 15 years. The commissioning of the system is planned for 2024.

The tram line will consist of 28 kilometers of double track with 29 stations, running between Lyngby, a northern suburb of Copenhagen, and Ishøj, a suburb south of the city. Each Avenio tram has a seating capacity of 64 and space for 199 standees. The line will run along the Ring 3 highway and replace bus service in an effort to decarbonize public transport as part of the urban development plan developed in 1947, known as the Finger Plan.

The purpose behind building a light rail system in Greater Copenhagen is to develop the city’s suburbs and connect the “fingers” to the capital and the 11 municipalities between them. This project will strengthen green transportation in Copenhagen and will mark a significant improvement in the city’s infrastructure. It will play an important role in improving air quality and reducing traffic jams and congestion in the capital1. Furthermore, it will support Copenhagen’s goal to become the world’s first carbon-neutral capital city by 2025.

fields.title: Stellantis J4U (Jeep COMPASS)
fields.description:
The Jeep COMPAS Project is a significant initiative by Stellantis for the Jeep brand. The project revolves around the development and production of the new Jeep Compass model. The new Compass is a completely new model, with major changes to those features and contents that are mostly appreciated by European customers: style, technology, safety, sustainability, and functionality.

This project marked the first Jeep launch in Europe for the Stellantis Group, and the new model is produced in Melfi, Italy. In Europe, Compass accounts for more than 40% of Jeep’s sales, and today one in four Compass vehicles sold is a plug-in hybrid model. The new Compass model offers a range of engines with lower CO2 emissions and fuel consumption, including the 4xe variants with plug-in hybrid technology.

The new Compass exterior and interior represent an expression of formal concepts, which will be found in upcoming Jeep models. It is more modern, technological, sophisticated, and with a stronger European flavor, while maintaining Jeep authenticity. The new model also debuts the Uconnect™ 5, the most advanced infotainment system ever in a Jeep vehicle, and Highway Assist, a driver assistance system for level 2 (L2) autonomous driving.

The new Compass targets “pragmatic dreamers”, rational customers who give importance to value and specs, but also look for a car able to answer to their emotional needs of freedom and adventure. By choosing the New Compass, owners receive access to the benefits of Jeep Wave, the brand’s new loyalty and customer care program.

The Jeep COMPAS Project is a significant step in the importance of the Jeep brand around the world and especially in Europe. It has been developed to speak a more European language, courtesy of the enhanced quality of the finishes and its advanced onboard technology1. It also introduces major new features that take it to an even higher level in terms of design, safety, technology, and functionality.
